questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have never travelled to Scotland, and I saw this as an opportunity to that. Also I've heard many good things about Scotland.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't really think I got that much information upon arrival. Most of the information I found by myself with no guidance

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would've liked more assistance upon arrival. When you travel to a country that you have never been to before you become very vulnerable and I would've liked some assistance during this process.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing in Glasgow. The whole housing situation is a big problem there and most students stay at hotels because the accomodation is very limited. The university of Strathclyde do not offer housing on campus to exchange students but only to other students. Me and my friend also got scammed by a landlord.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of scammers and try to use your network to find accomodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were a guide that explained how the registration process worked. Though this was time consuming.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At the fifth floor (if I remember correctly) there were two counselors for exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got registered in the classes I wanted to, so that was successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read all the mails and guides you recieve on KU mail from the host institution to complete the registration. These were quite helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses in Scotland is way more easy than in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly just classes where a professor talked about the reading we had to complete before the class. There were also 5 tutorials to each subject where you could discuss different dilemmas with other students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Property, Trusts, and Succession 
Law & Society 
Domestic Relations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the course: Domestic Relations because it was very interesting and the professor was also really good at explaining the different laws and point out the most important for the exam.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: As mentioned before me and my friend got scammed by a fake landowner and lost 8.700 DKK each which was an unexpected cost

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks on restaurants and bars are less expensive than I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the strathclyde union there were multiple social activities and also some only for exchange students. Students come there to study, to drink some beers before going out and there are different games you can play with your friends. During football VM it was possible to see every match at the union bar.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Follow the union on instagram, they post about different social activities during the semester. There are something for almost everyone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend using the weekends to explore Scotland which is apart of the whole experience. I planned multiple trips with esnstrathclyde  to the scottish highlands. This is a great opportunity to meet new people and also other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy to adjust, because the cultural differences aren't that big.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go on trips with esnstrathclyde and go to the events in the strath union at the learning and teaching building

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are really openminded and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make the most out of your exchange, this is a once in a life experience. Try to be openminded and talk to people even though it can be nerve wrecking

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the weekend trips to the highlands

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably to learn to understand the Scottish accent

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
